title: Two Consonants Together
overview:
No new letters today. You know them all.
Two consonants sit side by side.
Both of them are said: s - t - o - p.
Four sounds now, not three.
functions: Hear both consonants when they are side by side
Read a word with two consonants at the start
Read a word with two consonants at the end
Write a word that has four sounds
Tell two sounds from one sound
Read the tricky words there, here and were
learningPath: Words: twelve words with four sounds.
Patterns: the start, the end, one sound or two.
Write the words from their sounds.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 11. There is nothing new to learn.
No new letters. You know every one.
But the words get one sound longer.
Listen to the word stop.
s. t. o. p. Four sounds.
Look at the start. S and T.
Two letters, side by side.
Say them both. sss. t.
Not one sound. Two sounds, close together.
Now blend the word. s. t. o. p. Stop.
Careful here. Think back to Unit 8.
There, ck was two letters and ONE sound.
Here, st is two letters and TWO sounds.
Both are true. You must know which is which.
There is a way to tell. Use your ears.
Say the word slowly. Count what you hear.
Sack. sss. a. k. Three sounds.
Stop. sss. t. o. p. Four sounds.
Your ears know. Your eyes do not.
Now some more at the start.
Trip. t. r. i. p. Four sounds.
Clap. c. l. a. p. Four sounds.
Swim. s. w. i. m. Four sounds.
Drum. d. r. u. m. Flag. f. l. a. g.
They can come at the END too.
Desk. d. e. s. k. Listen to the end.
sss. k. Two sounds, both said.
Jump. j. u. m. p. Help. h. e. l. p.
Milk. Tent. Lift. All four sounds.
This is harder than it looks.
Not because it is new. Because it is longer.
Four sounds is more to hold in your head.
Go slowly. Say every sound. Then join them.
Three tricky words today. There. Here. Were.
Do not try to sound those out. Learn them.
That is Unit 11. Two letters, two sounds.

grammar.title: Two consonants, two sounds
grammar.explanation:
Two consonants can sit side by side.
Both of them are said.
Nothing is joined. Nothing is lost.
grammar.rule:
st  =  s  then  t
tr  =  t  then  r
cl  =  c  then  l
sw  =  s  then  w
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word stop.
1. Say the first sound. sss.
2. Say the next. t.
3. Now o. Now p.
4. Four sounds. Say them in order.
5. Join them. Stop.
grammar.mistake:
Do not leave one out.
Saying top for stop drops the s.
Say every sound you see.
grammar.practice:
Say both sounds for each pair.
1. st
2. tr
3. cl
4. sw
5. dr
6. fl
grammar.answers:
Check yourself out loud.
Did you say two sounds each time?
One sound is wrong here.

grammar.title: Two consonants at the start
grammar.explanation:
The pair comes before the vowel.
Say both, then the rest of the word.
grammar.rule:
stop   s - t - o - p
trip   t - r - i - p
clap   c - l - a - p
swim   s - w - i - m
drum   d - r - u - m
flag   f - l - a - g
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word clap.
1. c. Then l.
2. Do not stop between them.
3. Now the vowel. a.
4. Now the end. p.
5. Join it all. Clap.
grammar.mistake:
Adding a sound is the common slip.
Cuh-lap is five sounds. Clap is four.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. s - t - o - p
2. t - r - i - p
3. c - l - a - p
4. s - w - i - m
5. d - r - u - m
6. f - l - a - g
grammar.answers:
1. stop
2. trip
3. clap
4. swim
5. drum
6. flag
Five or six right? You can read these.

grammar.title: Two consonants at the end
grammar.explanation:
The pair comes after the vowel.
The end of the word has two sounds.
grammar.rule:
desk   d - e - s - k
jump   j - u - m - p
help   h - e - l - p
milk   m - i - l - k
tent   t - e - n - t
lift   l - i - f - t
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word desk.
1. d. Then e.
2. Now listen to the end.
3. sss. Then k.
4. Two sounds at the end.
5. Join it. Desk.
grammar.mistake:
The end gets dropped, not the start.
Des for desk loses the k.
Say the last sound out loud.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. d - e - s - k
2. j - u - m - p
3. h - e - l - p
4. m - i - l - k
5. t - e - n - t
6. l - i - f - t
grammar.answers:
1. desk
2. jump
3. help
4. milk
5. tent
6. lift
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: One sound or two? Ask your ears
grammar.explanation:
In Unit 8, ck was one sound.
Here, st is two sounds.
Both are true. Your ears tell you which.
grammar.rule:
sack   s - a - ck     3 sounds
stop   s - t - o - p   4 sounds

hill   h - i - ll      3 sounds
help   h - e - l - p   4 sounds
grammar.workedExample:
You see two letters together.
1. Do not look. Listen.
2. Say the word slowly.
3. Count what you HEAR.
4. One sound, or two?
5. Your ears decide, not your eyes.
grammar.mistake:
Counting letters gives the wrong answer.
Sack has four letters and three sounds.
Count sounds. Never count letters.
grammar.practice:
How many sounds? Count what you hear.
1. sack
2. stop
3. hill
4. help
5. miss
6. lift
grammar.answers:
1. three
2. four
3. three
4. four
5. three
6. four
The odd ones are 1, 3 and 5. Those are doubles.

speaking.instructions:

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — One or two?

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: Nothing new, and that is the difficulty
teacherNotes.note: There is not one new grapheme in this unit. Learners often expect it to be easy for that reason and find it hard, which reads to them as going backwards. Say plainly what changed: the words are one sound longer, and four sounds is more to hold in the head than three. It is a memory load, not a new fact.

teacherNotes.type: The dropped sound is the thing to listen for
teacherNotes.note: Two errors cover nearly everything you will hear. At the start, the first consonant goes — top for stop, lap for clap. At the end, the last one goes — des for desk, jum for jump. Do not correct the whole word. Say only the sound that went missing, and have them put it back.

teacherNotes.type: Do not let them insert a vowel
teacherNotes.note: Cuh-lap and suh-top are the other failure, and they come from saying the letter sounds too separately. The fix is speed, not accuracy: have them say the pair faster until the vowel disappears. Slow blending is right for reading a new word and wrong for practising a pair.

teacherNotes.type: Unit 8 has to be held at the same time
teacherNotes.note: This unit contradicts what Unit 8 taught, and both are true. Some learners will start sounding out sack as s-a-c-k again. The discrimination is the unit's own outcome, and the test is always the ear: say the word, count what you hear. Counting letters gives the wrong answer in both directions.

These three are close in sound and close in spelling, which is why they are together. Teach here and there as a pair by meaning — this place, that place — and point while you say them. Were is separate: it is simply the past of are.

assignment.title: Read and write the four-sound words
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Read these words twice.
stop, trip, clap, desk, jump, milk
Slowly the first time. Faster the second.
2. Write six words from their sounds.
Then write how many sounds each one has.
Listen back before you finish.
